title: 2026-11-05_Mirai_Worm_Investigation_abf
description: Security monitoring has detected unusual network activity originating from the internal network. Initial analysis suggests the presence of a Mirai worm variant targeting Linux-based devices. Your task is to investigate the compromised hosts, identify the malware's behavior, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected unusual network activity originating from the internal network. Initial analysis suggests the presence of a Mirai worm variant targeting Linux-based devices. Your task is to investigate the compromised hosts, identify the malware's behavior, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: SSH into the patient-zero host using the username 'analyst' and password 'Mirai2023!' and enter the passkey 'start'.
levels.local_content: SSH into the patient-zero host using the username 'analyst' and password 'Mirai2023!' and enter the passkey 'start'.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual CPU-intensive and network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the patient-zero host using the provided credentials.
2. List all running and inactive services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`.
3. Look for unfamiliar service names or misspellings of legitimate services.
4. Identify the service named `sysnet-monitor.service` as the suspicious service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is related to network monitoring.

levels.title: Identify Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the patient-zero host using the provided credentials.
2. Inspect the suspicious service using the command `systemctl cat sysnet-monitor.service`.
3. Identify the network port specified in the `ExecStart` line of the service file.
4. The port number is `52869`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl cat <service>` to inspect the service file.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service file.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The port number is specified in the script path.

levels.title: Identify Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Investigators suspect that a mechanism keeps the beaconing service running across reboots and process termination. Determine which system component is responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the patient-zero host using the provided credentials.
2. List all timers using the command `systemctl list-timers --all`.
3. Identify the timer named `sysnet-monitor.timer` as the suspicious timer.
4. The timer name is `sysnet-monitor.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious timer is related to the beaconing service.

levels.title: Identify Script Path
levels.content: After identifying the different activities of the malware, check how this worm dropped in the system. Identify the path of the script.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the patient-zero host using the provided credentials.
2. Check the bash history using the command `history`.
3. Identify the path of the script executed by the user.
4. The path of the script is `/opt/.worm/worm.sh`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `history` to check the bash history.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the path of the script executed by the user.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The script is located in the `/opt/.worm` directory.

levels.title: Investigate Spread Log
levels.content: Investigate the spread log to determine the IP addresses of the hosts that the worm has spread to.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the patient-zero host using the provided credentials.
2. Navigate to the worm directory using the command `cd /opt/.worm`.
3. Read the spread log using the command `cat spread.log`.
4. Identify the IP addresses of the hosts that the worm has spread to.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `cd /opt/.worm` to navigate to the worm directory.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `cat spread.log` to read the spread log.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for the IP addresses in the spread log.

levels.title: Analyze Beacon Log
levels.content: Analyze the beacon log to determine the frequency of beaconing activity.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the patient-zero host using the provided credentials.
2. Navigate to the worm directory using the command `cd /opt/.worm`.
3. Read the beacon log using the command `cat beacon.log`.
4. Determine the frequency of beaconing activity by analyzing the timestamps in the log.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `cd /opt/.worm` to navigate to the worm directory.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `cat beacon.log` to read the beacon log.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for the timestamps in the beacon log to determine the frequency of beaconing activity.

levels.title: Identify C2 Server
levels.content: Identify the command and control (C2) server that the worm is communicating with.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the patient-zero host using the provided credentials.
2. Navigate to the worm directory using the command `cd /opt/.worm`.
3. Read the worm script using the command `cat worm.sh`.
4. Identify the C2 server specified in the script.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `cd /opt/.worm` to navigate to the worm directory.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `cat worm.sh` to read the worm script.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for the C2 server specified in the script.

levels.title: Preserve Forensic Evidence
levels.content: Preserve forensic evidence by creating a backup of the worm-related files.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the patient-zero host using the provided credentials.
2. Navigate to the worm directory using the command `cd /opt/.worm`.
3. Create a backup of the worm-related files using the command `tar -czvf worm_backup.tar.gz *`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `cd /opt/.worm` to navigate to the worm directory.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `tar -czvf worm_backup.tar.gz *` to create a backup of the worm-related files.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Ensure that the backup file is created in the current directory.

levels.title: Contain the Threat
levels.content: Contain the threat by blocking unauthorized communication with the C2 server.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the patient-zero host using the provided credentials.
2. Block the C2 server's IP address using the command `iptables -A INPUT -s <C2_IP> -j DROP`.
3. Verify that the communication is blocked using the command `ss -tulnp`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `iptables -A INPUT -s <C2_IP> -j DROP` to block the C2 server's IP address.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Replace `<C2_IP>` with the actual IP address of the C2 server.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to verify that the communication is blocked.

levels.title: Terminate Malicious Process
levels.content: Terminate the malicious process responsible for the beaconing activity.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the patient-zero host using the provided credentials.
2. Identify the process ID (PID) of the malicious process using the command `ps aux | grep worm`.
3. Terminate the malicious process using the command `kill -9 <PID>`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ps aux | grep worm` to identify the process ID (PID) of the malicious process.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Replace `<PID>` with the actual process ID of the malicious process.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `kill -9 <PID>` to terminate the malicious process.

levels.title: Disable Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Disable the persistence mechanism to prevent the malicious service from restarting.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the patient-zero host using the provided credentials.
2. Disable the suspicious timer using the command `systemctl stop sysnet-monitor.timer`.
3. Disable the suspicious service using the command `systemctl stop sysnet-monitor.service`.
4. Verify that the timer and service are disabled using the command `systemctl list-timers --all` and `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl stop sysnet-monitor.timer` to disable the suspicious timer.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl stop sysnet-monitor.service` to disable the suspicious service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers --all` and `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to verify that the timer and service are disabled.

levels.title: Remove Malicious Artifacts
levels.content: Remove confirmed malicious artifacts without destroying preserved evidence.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the patient-zero host using the provided credentials.
2. Navigate to the worm directory using the command `cd /opt/.worm`.
3. Remove the worm-related files using the command `rm -rf *`.
4. Verify that the files are removed using the command `ls -lah`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `cd /opt/.worm` to navigate to the worm directory.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `rm -rf *` to remove the worm-related files.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ls -lah` to verify that the files are removed.

levels.title: Verify Malicious Activity
levels.content: Verify that malicious activity has ceased and required legitimate functionality remains operational.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the patient-zero host using the provided credentials.
2. Monitor network activity using the command `ss -tulnp`.
3. Verify that no unauthorized communication is occurring.
4. Check the system logs using the command `journalctl -xe`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to monitor network activity.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Verify that no unauthorized communication is occurring.

hints.title: Third hint title
